\item \textbf{How many series carry the gain} (Figure~\ref{fig:rh_ladder}). Following

  \rhldEBNDaysOrd{} ordinary days and the \rhldEBNDaysEv{} FOMC statement days of Section~\ref{sec:rh_fi}. Each model

question: On the every-bar ladder the linear readings change: all five models INTERMEDIATE on every bar (linear were CONCENTRATED monthly; k90 5 -> 10); top 10 beat the full set significantly only for the ridge (p .030 / .361 / .522); top 5 keep 78-87% and are significantly worse for lasso and elastic net; the best linear rung is 10-20. How should A_fi:388-411, 01_introduction:133-136 and 09_conclusion:46-50 state the linear result (and the trees' 'other series add little', now p .008 / .005)?
answer: Conditional on Q-2026-10-29-30's switch; if that is vetoed, this item lapses and the monthly text stays. State the linear result as the every-bar numbers show it, each significance claim with its test and no clause-final verdict tails (V6): the top 10 series keep at least the full set's gain in all three linear classes, significantly more only in the ridge (nominal p, as everywhere else in the paper); the top 5 keep less, significantly less in the lasso and the elastic net; the pre-specified reading is intermediate in all five models. 'Concentrated' is no longer said of the ladder, and 'do best with N series' goes. The boosted trees' remainder beyond the top 10 is small but significant, with its tests; the forest's monthly result is one labelled sentence. The introduction and conclusion print the linear range next to the trees', carry no p-value, and say the gain sits in about \ladderEBTopK{} of the \rhldEBNSeries{} series instead of 'a few series'. The headings ('The gain is concentrated, not dense and weak'; 'The gain is concentrated') stay: they rest on the group ablations. The 'Ridge against lasso' bullet (A_fi.tex:403-408) is unchanged. Replacement text for 01_introduction.tex:133-138, 09_conclusion.tex:46-50 and A_fi.tex:385-414, and the generator's new macros and checks, are in actions[].detail; the old text is parked in dated comments.
answer_short: Ladder sentences on every-bar numbers: top 10 keep 96-97% of the boosted trees' gain and 104-115% of the linear models'; gain in about 10 of 46 series; 'concentrated', 'do best' dropped.
